beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Kavya, and this video is about OpenTelemetry for AI agents. Quick note: the voice you're hearing is AI, Kokoro text-to-speech reading a script I wrote and checked. When an agent gives a wrong answer, the log usually says it finished, and that something looked off. So what would it take to see which step actually broke?

props.command: My research agent answered with a citation that doesn't exist. The log just says it finished and the citation wasn't found. How do I see which step actually broke?

beats.narration_text: Here's the idea: OpenTelemetry for agents isn't more logging. It records every step as a linked, timed span, so a wrong answer comes with the path that produced it.

props.text:
Agent tracing is just more logging.
Each step, timed and linked.

beats.narration_text: Strip OpenTelemetry for agents down and it's four parts. Spans: one per model call, tool call, or retrieval. Trace context, which links every span in one run. Attributes, the structured facts on each span, like tokens, tool name, or hit count. And exporters, so the same trace opens in whichever backend you use. None of it is tied to one vendor.

beats.narration_text: So I ran it. A scripted research agent gets asked about churn in the Q3 report. Here's what a plain log keeps: it finished in about two point four seconds, it answered that churn fell to three point one percent, and it warned the citation wasn't found. Which step failed? The log never recorded it.

beats.narration_text: To be fair, tracing shows the failure. It doesn't fix it; you still have to correct that index name. It also only sees what you instrumented: a step without a span is invisible. And my demo used a scripted agent and a small tracer shaped like OpenTelemetry, not the real SDK. What it does give you: which step broke, where the time went, and what each call returned.

beats.narration_text: Recap. OpenTelemetry for agents is spans, trace context, attributes, and exporters. The plain log said the run finished, with one warning. The trace showed the search call returning zero hits in eleven milliseconds, and the answer citing a page anyway. The boundary: it finds the failure, it doesn't fix it. So before you blame the model, trace the run.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Ask Claude exactly this: look at the last agent failure I couldn't explain. Help me add OpenTelemetry spans around each model call, tool call, and retrieval step, with the attributes I'd need to find it next time. Watch which attributes it suggests. Hit counts and token use are the ones that catch quiet failures.
